title: Credential dumping
overview: Triage a Sysmon process access record involving the authentication subsystem.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: LSASS Memory
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: Memory-read access to LSASS from an unverified caller warrants examination of the process and endpoint evidence.
evidence: Inspect source and target process, normalized access class and publisher. Check whether other records show suspicious output.
false_positive: Approved security tooling can legitimately inspect sensitive processes.
tuning: Use a verified publisher and deployed product identity for exceptions. Review vendor releases that change access behavior.
response: Preserve endpoint evidence, isolate if supporting evidence exists and assess credential exposure before rotation.
prevention: Enable Credential Guard and LSASS protection where appropriate and audit their status.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The sample contains process-access metadata, with no dump, memory content or credential extraction.

questions.prompt: Which target makes the behavior sensitive?
Can the observation alone identify exposed credentials?
options: Every read event proves credentials were collected
questions.explanation: Process access is an indicator. Scope exposure from corroborating artifacts.
